newsitem.title: UK: Balanced aluminium to precede bull market - MBR.
newsitem.headline: Balanced aluminium to precede bull market - MBR.

text.p: The aluminium market will broadly be in balance this year and initially in 1998, which will subsequently allow for bull market conditions to emerge, Metal Bulletin Research (MBR) said.
In a special report on the aluminium market, MBR said that demand will rebound in 1997 and 1998 after a weak period during much of 1995 and 1996.
"In tandem, however, we expect continued strong growth in western world production which will restrain prices," MBR analyst Raju Daswani said.
Prices will also be capped by a continued high level of exports from the former Eastern countries.
"We are forecasting a total of 2.1 million tonnes being the net shipments into the West over this year, with a larger drop to 1.8 million tonnes taking place next year," MBR said.
This will result in aluminium roughly in balance over the next two years in supply/demand terms, precluding any bull run till mid to late 1998 at the earliest.
But MBR said that improving demand will boost sentiment and allow prices to consolidate at current levels, tracking higher, albeit slowly.
Looking at demand, MBR said that higher levels in the U.S. and Europe will feed through to overall Western World consumption growth of 4.6 percent this year.

On the production side expansions later this year in Australia, India and Iceland, new greenfield starts in Iran and Nigeria, and possible re-starts of idled capacity should see a 4.6 percent rise in Western output in 1997.
But after further increases in early 1998, there is little new greenfield or brownfield capacity scheduled. So output growth will ease in subsequent years, MBR said.
By late 1998 and early 1999 metal supply will tighten, and the market move into a large deficit, with investment fund activity seen boosting aluminium prices prior to this.
MBR said prices will average $1,640 and $1,870 a tonne for 1997 and 1998 respectively, peaking in 1999 at over $2,300 a tonne.
